TypeComment.summary: Anything that can appear in a run of content: an element, a text run, an interpolation, a control-flow directive, a code block or a style block. Content is the one list shape the grammar has, and every member of it derives from here.
The right-hand side of an attribute: either a quoted run that may mix literal text with interpolations, or a bare expression written without quotes.
A file-level header: @component, @namespace, @tag or @using.
TypeComment.remarks: ⚠ They share a base so that they can share a list, and they share a list so that the tree holds them in the order the file wrote them. Held as one field each — which is what this was — a node's children come out in *field* order, so a file that put its @using above its @namespace did not reproduce itself. That is the one property everything else here rests on: an incremental reparse, a formatter and every span-to-source mapping all assume a tree can be printed back into the file it came from.

PropertyComment.summary: Every file-level header, in the order the file wrote them.
PropertyComment.remarks: One list rather than a field each, so that the tree prints back into its file whatever order the headers were written in. , , and read it.

PropertyComment.summary: Everything after the headers: markup, code blocks and style blocks.

TypeComment.summary: A whole .vxml file. The root of every VXML tree.

PropertyComment.summary: The generated partial class's name.

TypeComment.summary: @component Counter — the file's one required header.

PropertyComment.summary: The static in @using static System.Math, which makes a type whose static members are imported rather than a namespace.
The name on the left of the = in @using Prefab = A.B.Prefab. Absent for a plain import, which is what makes mean the same thing either way.
A dotted namespace — or, with an alias, the type or namespace it names — carried whole as one token.

TypeComment.summary: @using Vixen.Ui.Controls, @using Prefab = A.B.Prefab or @using static System.Math — copied verbatim into the generated file.
TypeComment.remarks: ⚠ The alias is stored ahead of the name, not instead of it. Held as one Name that meant the alias when there was one, every reader of a using had to know which shape it was looking at — and the emitter, which does not, wrote using Prefab; for the aliased form and left the author with a CS0246 on a line they never typed.

PropertyComment.summary: A dotted namespace, carried whole as one token.

TypeComment.summary: @namespace Game.Screens — where the generated class goes.
TypeComment.remarks: ⚠ The file wins over the project. A generator that has a root namespace to offer supplies it as a default, and this overrides it — which is the point: a component in a folder whose name is not what its namespace should be has no other way to say so, and renaming the folder is not a fix a library can rely on.

PropertyComment.summary: An element name, hyphens and all.

TypeComment.summary: @tag task-center — the element name the component's host answers to.
TypeComment.remarks: ⚠ A header rather than three lines of @code. The default is the type's name in lower case and it cannot produce a hyphen, so every component whose stylesheet spells its tag the way CSS does — which is every compound one — would otherwise have to override a virtual property to say a single word. What a component is called is a property of the component, and the file already has a place where a component says what it is.

PropertyComment.summary: A type name, dotted, carried whole as one token.
PropertyComment.remarks: ⚠ Nothing here resolves it, and the emitter writes it where a base type goes under its own #line. So a base that does not exist, one that is sealed and one that is neither a component nor an element are all reported by Roslyn against the characters in the .vxml — the same bargain the tag name is emitted under, and the reason this side needs no semantic model to have gained a second kind of output.

TypeComment.summary: @inherits Vixen.Ui.Controls.Control — what the generated class derives from.
TypeComment.remarks: Absent means Component, which is what a .vxml is for. Present means the file is describing a UiElement instead: a type callers hold, put in a tree with Add<T>, and find with a walk — everything a component is not, and the reason four of the editor's six panels could not be markup.

PropertyComment.summary: The ambient key, dotted, carried whole as one token.
PropertyComment.remarks: ⚠ It is the key and not the value's class. Inject<T> matches on the type argument, so this has to be the same type the provider wrote — an interface, usually. Nothing here resolves it: the emitter writes it where a type goes, under its own #line, so a name that is not a type is Roslyn's error on the characters after @inject.

PropertyComment.summary: What the generated property is called.
PropertyComment.remarks: ⚠ Written out rather than derived from the type. A type name is not a member name — ITheme would give ITheme, and stripping an I is a convention rather than a rule — and a file injecting two values of related types needs to be able to say which is which.

TypeComment.summary: @inject ITheme Theme — the property that reads an ambient value.
TypeComment.remarks: ⚠ Sugar over one line of code-behind, and the mirror of <provide>. It generates private ITheme? Theme => Inject<ITheme>(); and nothing else, so the property is nullable because injection can find nothing — a consumer that needs a fallback still writes the ?? Default in @code. Repeatable, like @using and unlike every other header, because the shape it is for is a file that reads three ambient values.

PropertyComment.summary: The C# between the braces, verbatim and unparsed.

TypeComment.summary: @code { … }. VXML never parses C#: the body travels as one token and Roslyn is the only thing that ever reads it.
A braced run of content — the body of an @if, an @for or an else. Braces rather than Razor's } sentinels, per ADR-009.

PropertyComment.summary: > for an element with content, /> for a self-closing one — which is also what says whether should exist.

TypeComment.summary: An opening or self-closing tag with its attributes.
A closing tag.

PropertyComment.summary: Absent when the tag closed itself — and also when the file did not close it at all, which is what makes an unclosed element a recoverable parse rather than a lost one.

TypeComment.summary: An element. A lowercase name is an intrinsic; a name starting with an uppercase letter is a component. The parser does not care which — the binder does.

PropertyComment.summary: Everything up to </style>, verbatim. VCSS parses it, not VXML.

TypeComment.summary: <style scoped>…</style>. A separate node rather than an element because its content is not markup and must never be lexed as such.

PropertyComment.summary: The whole name including any : and . — on:click.stop is one token, and splitting it is the binder's job.
Absent for a valueless attribute such as scoped.

TypeComment.summary: One attribute on a tag.

PropertyComment.summary: Text and interpolations, interleaved — so class="btn @variant" is one value with two parts rather than a string the binder has to re-scan.

TypeComment.summary: A quoted attribute value. Single and double quotes are both accepted.
An unquoted @expr value, as in step=@Step.
A run of literal text. Whitespace that spans a line break never reaches here — the lexer makes it trivia, so indentation is formatting and a space you typed is content.

PropertyComment.summary: The C# expression, verbatim. Its span is what a #line maps back to.

TypeComment.summary: @expr — an implicit expression, or a parenthesised one after @(.
@if (cond) { … } else { … }.

PropertyComment.summary: A for a plain else, or an for else if — which is how the chain nests.

TypeComment.summary: The else arm of an @if.

PropertyComment.summary: The , before an index name, absent when the loop declares none.

The name bound to the row's position, from @for (var row, i in Rows). ⚠ It is a Signal<int> rather than an int, because a surviving key keeps its region and its body is never re-run — so a captured position would be a lie from the first reorder.
The @empty of @for (…) { … } @empty { … }, absent when the loop declares no fallback arm.

What the loop draws instead of rows. ⚠ Two fields rather than the clause node else has: an else chains — its body is an IfSyntax for else if — and an @empty cannot, so a node of its own would buy a public type and no structure.

TypeComment.summary: @for (var i in sequence) { … } — the keyed reconciler's input.
@switch (subject) { case pattern: … default: … }.

PropertyComment.summary: case or default.
The C# pattern, verbatim; absent on default. Emitted between case and : without being understood.

TypeComment.summary: One arm of an @switch.
